questions.question: ___! I completely forgot to bring my admission ticket to the testing center.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Oops' expresses a mild apology or realization of a small mistake. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Oops' digunakan untuk menyatakan permintaan maaf ringan atau kesadaran akan kesalahan kecil.
details_explanation.introduction: Interjections express sudden emotion or reaction. 'Oops' is used after a minor mistake or accident.

rules.title: 1. Use of Oops
rules.explanation: Use 'Oops' when you realize you made a small mistake or forgot something.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'Oops' saat menyadari kesalahan kecil atau lupa sesuatu.

common_mistakes.wrong: Ouch! I forgot my ticket.
common_mistakes.correct: Oops! I forgot my ticket.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Ouch' expresses pain, not a minor mistake. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Ouch' menyatakan rasa sakit, bukan kesalahan kecil.

other_examples.sentence: 1. Oops! I dropped my pen.
other_examples.translation: Ups! Saya menjatuhkan pena saya.

other_examples.sentence: 2. Oops! I called the wrong number.
other_examples.translation: Ups! Saya menelepon nomor yang salah.

questions.question: The sergeant ordered the recruits ___ their boots immediately before the inspection.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Order' can take an object + to-infinitive: order someone to do something. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Order' dapat diikuti objek + to-infinitive: memerintahkan seseorang untuk melakukan sesuatu.
details_explanation.introduction: Verbs such as order, tell, ask, and advise commonly use the pattern verb + object + to-infinitive.

rules.title: 1. Object + To-Infinitive
rules.explanation: After 'order', use the object followed by 'to + base verb'.
notes: ID: Setelah 'order', gunakan objek lalu 'to + kata kerja dasar'.

common_mistakes.wrong: The sergeant ordered the recruits polish their boots.
common_mistakes.correct: The sergeant ordered the recruits to polish their boots.
common_mistakes.reason: English: The object complement after 'order' needs a to-infinitive. Bahasa Indonesia: Object complement setelah 'order' memerlukan to-infinitive.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The teacher ordered the students to be quiet.
other_examples.translation: Guru memerintahkan para siswa untuk diam.

other_examples.sentence: 2. The officer ordered them to stop.
other_examples.translation: Petugas memerintahkan mereka untuk berhenti.

questions.question: The cadet ___ his uniform neatly before the morning inspection every day.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The singular subject 'cadet' takes 'irons' in the simple present for a daily habit. Bahasa Indonesia: Subjek tunggal 'cadet' memakai 'irons' dalam simple present untuk kebiasaan harian.
details_explanation.introduction: The simple present describes habits, routines, and general facts.

rules.title: 1. Third-Person Singular
rules.explanation: Add -s or -es to the base verb with he, she, it, or a singular noun.
notes: ID: Tambahkan -s/-es pada kata kerja dasar dengan subjek tunggal orang ketiga.

common_mistakes.wrong: The cadet iron his uniform every day.
common_mistakes.correct: The cadet irons his uniform every day.
common_mistakes.reason: English: The third-person singular subject requires 'irons'. Bahasa Indonesia: Subjek tunggal orang ketiga memerlukan 'irons'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. She cleans her room every morning.
other_examples.translation: Dia membersihkan kamarnya setiap pagi.

other_examples.sentence: 2. The soldier checks his equipment daily.
other_examples.translation: Prajurit itu memeriksa perlengkapannya setiap hari.

questions.question: ___ you ever taken a standardized English proficiency test before applying to university?

details_explanation.explanation: English: Use 'Have' with 'you' in the present perfect to ask about life experience with 'ever'. Bahasa Indonesia: Gunakan 'Have' dengan 'you' dalam present perfect untuk menanyakan pengalaman hidup dengan 'ever'.
details_explanation.introduction: The present perfect with 'ever' asks whether an experience has happened at any time before now.

rules.title: 1. Have/Has + Ever + Past Participle
rules.explanation: Use 'Have' with I/you/we/they and 'Has' with he/she/it.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'Have' untuk I/you/we/they dan 'Has' untuk he/she/it.

common_mistakes.wrong: Did you ever taken the test?
common_mistakes.correct: Have you ever taken the test?
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Ever' with experience uses the present perfect, not 'did + past participle'. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Ever' untuk pengalaman memakai present perfect, bukan 'did + past participle'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. Have you ever visited Bali?
other_examples.translation: Apakah kamu pernah mengunjungi Bali?

other_examples.sentence: 2. Has she ever failed an exam?
other_examples.translation: Apakah dia pernah gagal ujian?

questions.question: The children are waiting ___ for their exam results to be announced by the school.

details_explanation.explanation: English: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'are waiting'; 'anxiously' describes how they wait. Bahasa Indonesia: Kata keterangan diperlukan untuk memodifikasi kata kerja 'are waiting'; 'anxiously' menjelaskan cara mereka menunggu.
details_explanation.introduction: Adverbs of manner describe how an action is performed.

rules.title: 1. Adverb Modifies Verb
rules.explanation: Use an adverb of manner after the verb or after the object to describe how the action happens.
notes: ID: Gunakan adverb of manner untuk menjelaskan bagaimana aksi dilakukan.

common_mistakes.wrong: The children are waiting anxious.
common_mistakes.correct: The children are waiting anxiously.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Anxious' is an adjective; 'anxiously' is the adverb modifying 'waiting'. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Anxious' adalah adjective; 'anxiously' adalah adverb yang memodifikasi 'waiting'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. She spoke quietly during the meeting.
other_examples.translation: Dia berbicara dengan tenang selama rapat.

other_examples.sentence: 2. They waited patiently for the announcement.
other_examples.translation: Mereka menunggu dengan sabar untuk pengumuman itu.

questions.question: The principal gave ___ a warning about the strict school rules yesterday.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The verb 'gave' needs an object pronoun; 'them' is the object form for a plural recipient. Bahasa Indonesia: Kata kerja 'gave' memerlukan object pronoun; 'them' adalah bentuk objek untuk penerima jamak.
details_explanation.introduction: Object pronouns receive the action of a verb.

rules.title: 1. Object Pronoun
rules.explanation: Use me, you, him, her, it, us, or them after a verb or preposition.
notes: ID: Gunakan me, you, him, her, it, us, atau them setelah kata kerja atau preposisi.

common_mistakes.wrong: The principal gave they a warning.
common_mistakes.correct: The principal gave them a warning.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'They' is a subject pronoun; 'them' is the object pronoun. Bahasa Indonesia: 'They' adalah subject pronoun; 'them' adalah object pronoun.

other_examples.sentence: 1. I saw them at the library.
other_examples.translation: Saya melihat mereka di perpustakaan.

other_examples.sentence: 2. She called us yesterday.
other_examples.translation: Dia menelepon kami kemarin.

questions.question: They have lived in Jakarta ___ five years while attending the state university.

details_explanation.explanation: English: Use 'for' with a length of time in the present perfect. Bahasa Indonesia: Gunakan 'for' dengan durasi waktu dalam present perfect.
details_explanation.introduction: The present perfect uses 'for' for a period of time and 'since' for a starting point.

rules.title: 1. For + Duration
rules.explanation: Use 'for' before expressions like five years, two months, or a long time.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'for' sebelum durasi seperti five years, two months, atau a long time.

common_mistakes.wrong: They have lived in Jakarta since five years.
common_mistakes.correct: They have lived in Jakarta for five years.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Since' needs a starting point, not a duration. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Since' memerlukan titik awal, bukan durasi.

other_examples.sentence: 1. I have studied English for three years.
other_examples.translation: Saya telah belajar bahasa Inggris selama tiga tahun.

other_examples.sentence: 2. She has worked here for six months.
other_examples.translation: Dia telah bekerja di sini selama enam bulan.

questions.question: ___ the fact that he was sick, he attended the crucial briefing for the new recruits.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Despite' is a preposition meaning 'in spite of' and is followed by a noun phrase. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Despite' adalah preposisi yang berarti 'meskipun' dan diikuti frasa kata benda.
details_explanation.introduction: Despite and in spite of are prepositions used before nouns or noun phrases to show contrast.

rules.title: 1. Despite + Noun Phrase
rules.explanation: Use 'Despite' before a noun, pronoun, or noun phrase such as 'the fact that...'.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'Despite' sebelum kata benda, pronoun, atau frasa kata benda.

common_mistakes.wrong: Although the fact that he was sick, he attended.
common_mistakes.correct: Despite the fact that he was sick, he attended.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Although' is followed by a clause, not a noun phrase. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Although' diikuti klausa, bukan frasa kata benda.

other_examples.sentence: 1. Despite the rain, they continued the march.
other_examples.translation: Meskipun hujan, mereka melanjutkan pawai.

other_examples.sentence: 2. Despite his age, he passed the physical test.
other_examples.translation: Meskipun usianya, dia lulus tes fisik.

questions.question: ___! That was a very difficult mathematics question on the state university entrance exam.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Wow' expresses surprise or admiration. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Wow' mengekspresikan kejutan atau kekaguman.
details_explanation.introduction: Interjections such as 'Wow' express strong reaction to something impressive or surprising.

rules.title: 1. Wow for Surprise
rules.explanation: Use 'Wow' when reacting to something surprising, impressive, or difficult.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'Wow' saat bereaksi terhadap sesuatu yang mengejutkan, mengesankan, atau sulit.

common_mistakes.wrong: Ouch! That was a difficult question.
common_mistakes.correct: Wow! That was a difficult question.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Ouch' shows pain, not surprise or admiration. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Ouch' menunjukkan rasa sakit, bukan kejutan atau kekaguman.

other_examples.sentence: 1. Wow! You finished the exam so quickly.
other_examples.translation: Wah! Kamu menyelesaikan ujiannya begitu cepat.

other_examples.sentence: 2. Wow! That was an amazing performance.
other_examples.translation: Wah! Itu adalah penampilan yang luar biasa.

questions.question: The final interview for the military academy will begin ___ 8:00 AM tomorrow.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'At' is used with exact clock times. Bahasa Indonesia: 'At' digunakan dengan waktu jam yang tepat.
details_explanation.introduction: Prepositions of time include at for exact times, on for days/dates, and in for months/years/long periods.

rules.title: 1. At + Exact Time
rules.explanation: Use 'at' before clock times such as 8:00 AM, noon, or midnight.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'at' sebelum waktu jam seperti 8:00 AM, noon, atau midnight.

common_mistakes.wrong: The interview will begin in 8:00 AM.
common_mistakes.correct: The interview will begin at 8:00 AM.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'In' is not used with an exact clock time. Bahasa Indonesia: 'In' tidak digunakan dengan waktu jam yang tepat.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The ceremony starts at 7:30 AM.
other_examples.translation: Upacara dimulai pukul 7:30 pagi.

other_examples.sentence: 2. We will meet at noon.
other_examples.translation: Kita akan bertemu pada tengah hari.

questions.question: The scientist made a remarkable ___ in the field of renewable energy.

details_explanation.explanation: English: A noun is needed after the adjective 'remarkable'; 'discovery' is the noun form. Bahasa Indonesia: Kata benda diperlukan setelah adjective 'remarkable'; 'discovery' adalah bentuk kata bendanya.
details_explanation.introduction: Suffixes such as -y, -ance, -ation, -ment, and -ness can form nouns.

rules.title: 1. Noun after Adjective
rules.explanation: Use a noun after an adjective such as 'remarkable'.
notes: ID: Gunakan kata benda setelah adjective seperti 'remarkable'.

common_mistakes.wrong: The scientist made a remarkable discover.
common_mistakes.correct: The scientist made a remarkable discovery.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Discover' is a verb; 'discovery' is the noun. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Discover' adalah kata kerja; 'discovery' adalah kata benda.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The discovery changed modern medicine.
other_examples.translation: Penemuan itu mengubah kedokteran modern.

other_examples.sentence: 2. They announced a major discovery in physics.
other_examples.translation: Mereka mengumumkan penemuan besar dalam fisika.

questions.question: The witness provided a highly ___ testimony during the criminal trial.

details_explanation.explanation: English: An adjective is needed to modify 'testimony'; 'believable' means able to be believed. Bahasa Indonesia: Adjective diperlukan untuk memodifikasi 'testimony'; 'believable' berarti dapat dipercaya.
details_explanation.introduction: The suffix -able forms adjectives meaning 'can be' or 'capable of being'.

rules.title: 1. Adjective before Noun
rules.explanation: Use an adjective before the noun it describes.
notes: ID: Gunakan adjective sebelum kata benda yang dijelaskannya.

common_mistakes.wrong: The witness provided a highly belief testimony.
common_mistakes.correct: The witness provided a highly believable testimony.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Belief' is a noun; 'believable' is the adjective. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Belief' adalah kata benda; 'believable' adalah adjective.

other_examples.sentence: 1. Her story was believable.
other_examples.translation: Ceritanya dapat dipercaya.

other_examples.sentence: 2. He gave a believable explanation.
other_examples.translation: Dia memberikan penjelasan yang dapat dipercaya.

questions.question: I have wanted to become a police officer ___ I was a young child.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Since' is used with a specific starting point in the past in the present perfect. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Since' digunakan dengan titik awal tertentu di masa lalu dalam present perfect.
details_explanation.introduction: The present perfect uses 'since' before a point in time and 'for' before a duration.

rules.title: 1. Since + Starting Point
rules.explanation: Use 'since' before a clause or time expression showing when something began.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'since' sebelum klausa atau ekspresi waktu yang menunjukkan kapan sesuatu dimulai.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have wanted to become a police officer for I was a child.
common_mistakes.correct: I have wanted to become a police officer since I was a child.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'For' is used with a duration, not a starting clause. Bahasa Indonesia: 'For' digunakan dengan durasi, bukan klausa titik awal.

other_examples.sentence: 1. She has lived here since 2019.
other_examples.translation: Dia telah tinggal di sini sejak 2019.

other_examples.sentence: 2. I have known him since we were children.
other_examples.translation: Saya telah mengenalnya sejak kami masih anak-anak.

questions.question: The new regulation is applicable ___ all state school students without exception.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The adjective 'applicable' is followed by the preposition 'to'. Bahasa Indonesia: Adjective 'applicable' diikuti preposisi 'to'.
details_explanation.introduction: Some adjectives have fixed prepositions, such as applicable to, responsible for, and interested in.

rules.title: 1. Applicable To
rules.explanation: Use 'applicable to' to mean relevant to or affecting someone/something.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'applicable to' untuk berarti berlaku bagi seseorang/sesuatu.

common_mistakes.wrong: The rule is applicable for all students.
common_mistakes.correct: The rule is applicable to all students.
common_mistakes.reason: English: The fixed preposition after 'applicable' is 'to'. Bahasa Indonesia: Preposisi tetap setelah 'applicable' adalah 'to'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. This rule is applicable to all employees.
other_examples.translation: Peraturan ini berlaku untuk semua karyawan.

other_examples.sentence: 2. The discount is applicable to new members.
other_examples.translation: Diskon tersebut berlaku untuk anggota baru.

questions.question: The unexpected ___ of the old documents made the historical research very difficult.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Disappearance' is the noun formed with dis- and -ance, meaning the act of vanishing. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Disappearance' adalah kata benda dengan dis- dan -ance, berarti tindakan menghilang.
details_explanation.introduction: Prefixes change meaning, and suffixes can change word class.

rules.title: 1. Noun after Adjective
rules.explanation: The adjective 'unexpected' modifies a noun, so use 'disappearance'.
notes: ID: Adjective 'unexpected' memodifikasi kata benda, jadi gunakan 'disappearance'.

common_mistakes.wrong: The unexpected disappear of the documents...
common_mistakes.correct: The unexpected disappearance of the documents...
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Disappear' is a verb; 'disappearance' is the noun. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Disappear' adalah kata kerja; 'disappearance' adalah kata benda.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The disappearance of the files shocked everyone.
other_examples.translation: Hilangnya berkas-berkas itu mengejutkan semua orang.

other_examples.sentence: 2. Police investigated the sudden disappearance of the witness.
other_examples.translation: Polisi menyelidiki hilangnya saksi secara mendadak.

questions.question: He is not tall enough to join the military police, ___ he has excellent leadership skills.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'But' connects two contrasting ideas. Bahasa Indonesia: 'But' menghubungkan dua ide yang bertentangan.
details_explanation.introduction: Coordinating conjunctions include and, but, or, so, and yet.

rules.title: 1. But for Contrast
rules.explanation: Use 'but' to show a contrast between two clauses.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'but' untuk menunjukkan kontras antara dua klausa.

common_mistakes.wrong: He is not tall, therefore he has leadership skills.
common_mistakes.correct: He is not tall, but he has leadership skills.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Therefore' shows result, not contrast. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Therefore' menunjukkan hasil, bukan kontras.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The test was hard, but she passed.
other_examples.translation: Ujian itu sulit, tetapi dia lulus.

other_examples.sentence: 2. He is young, but he is very experienced.
other_examples.translation: Dia muda, tetapi dia sangat berpengalaman.

questions.question: The task was extremely difficult, ___ the students managed to finish it on time.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'But' shows contrast between difficulty and successful completion. Bahasa Indonesia: 'But' menunjukkan kontras antara kesulitan dan keberhasilan menyelesaikan.
details_explanation.introduction: Use 'but' to connect a surprising or contrasting result.

rules.title: 1. But for Unexpected Result
rules.explanation: Use 'but' when the second clause contrasts with the first.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'but' ketika klausa kedua bertentangan dengan klausa pertama.

common_mistakes.wrong: The task was difficult, so the students managed to finish it.
common_mistakes.correct: The task was difficult, but the students managed to finish it.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'So' shows result, not contrast. Bahasa Indonesia: 'So' menunjukkan hasil, bukan kontras.

other_examples.sentence: 1. It was raining, but they continued the match.
other_examples.translation: Hujan turun, tetapi mereka melanjutkan pertandingan.

other_examples.sentence: 2. The road was long, but we arrived on time.
other_examples.translation: Jalannya panjang, tetapi kami tiba tepat waktu.

questions.question: The university awarded ___ a full scholarship for her outstanding academic achievements.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Awarded' needs an indirect object pronoun; 'her' is the correct object form. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Awarded' memerlukan indirect object pronoun; 'her' adalah bentuk objek yang tepat.
details_explanation.introduction: Indirect objects often receive something in verbs like give, award, send, and hand.

rules.title: 1. Indirect Object Pronoun
rules.explanation: Use object pronouns after verbs that take an indirect object.
notes: ID: Gunakan object pronoun setelah kata kerja yang memerlukan indirect object.

common_mistakes.wrong: The university awarded she a scholarship.
common_mistakes.correct: The university awarded her a scholarship.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'She' is a subject pronoun; 'her' is the object pronoun. Bahasa Indonesia: 'She' adalah subject pronoun; 'her' adalah object pronoun.

other_examples.sentence: 1. They gave her a prize.
other_examples.translation: Mereka memberinya hadiah.

other_examples.sentence: 2. The school sent him a letter.
other_examples.translation: Sekolah mengiriminya surat.

questions.question: She answers the interview questions ___ than her peers during the selection process.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The comparative adverb 'more confidently' modifies 'answers' and compares her with her peers. Bahasa Indonesia: Adverb komparatif 'more confidently' memodifikasi 'answers' dan membandingkannya dengan rekan-rekannya.
details_explanation.introduction: Adverbs of manner form the comparative with 'more' + adverb, especially adverbs ending in -ly.

rules.title: 1. Comparative Adverb
rules.explanation: Use 'more + adverb' for comparison with -ly adverbs.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'more + adverb' untuk perbandingan pada adverb berakhiran -ly.

common_mistakes.wrong: She answers more confident than her peers.
common_mistakes.correct: She answers more confidently than her peers.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Confident' is an adjective; the verb needs the adverb 'confidently'. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Confident' adalah adjective; kata kerja memerlukan adverb 'confidently'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. He speaks more clearly than before.
other_examples.translation: Dia berbicara lebih jelas daripada sebelumnya.

other_examples.sentence: 2. They work more efficiently than the other team.
other_examples.translation: Mereka bekerja lebih efisien daripada tim lain.

questions.question: This is the textbook ___ we use for our English grammar class this semester.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Which' refers to things such as a textbook. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Which' merujuk pada benda seperti buku teks.
details_explanation.introduction: Relative pronouns introduce adjective clauses: who for people, which for things, where for places.

rules.title: 1. Which for Things
rules.explanation: Use 'which' to refer to an object or thing in a relative clause.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'which' untuk merujuk benda dalam relative clause.

common_mistakes.wrong: This is the textbook who we use.
common_mistakes.correct: This is the textbook which we use.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Who' refers to people, not things. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Who' merujuk orang, bukan benda.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The book which I bought is interesting.
other_examples.translation: Buku yang saya beli itu menarik.

other_examples.sentence: 2. This is the phone which he lost.
other_examples.translation: Ini adalah ponsel yang dia hilangkan.

questions.question: This is the ___ military academy in the entire country.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Most prestigious' is the superlative form comparing one academy with all others. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Most prestigious' adalah bentuk superlatif yang membandingkan satu akademi dengan semua yang lain.
details_explanation.introduction: Superlatives compare one member of a group with the whole group.

rules.title: 1. Superlative Adjective
rules.explanation: Use 'the most + adjective' for long adjectives in superlative comparisons.
rules.structure: the most + adjective + noun + in/of + group
notes: ID: Gunakan 'the most + adjective' untuk adjective panjang dalam perbandingan superlatif.

common_mistakes.wrong: This is the more prestigious academy in the country.
common_mistakes.correct: This is the most prestigious academy in the country.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'More' is comparative; 'most' is superlative. Bahasa Indonesia: 'More' adalah komparatif; 'most' adalah superlatif.

other_examples.sentence: 1. She is the most talented student in the class.
other_examples.translation: Dia adalah siswa paling berbakat di kelas.

other_examples.sentence: 2. This is the most expensive hotel in the city.
other_examples.translation: Ini adalah hotel paling mahal di kota.

questions.question: ___ the strict requirements, hundreds of students applied for the prestigious scholarship.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Despite' introduces a contrast and is followed by a noun phrase. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Despite' memperkenalkan kontras dan diikuti frasa kata benda.
details_explanation.introduction: Despite and in spite of are prepositions of contrast.

rules.title: 1. Despite + Noun Phrase
rules.explanation: Use 'Despite' before a noun phrase, not before a full clause.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'Despite' sebelum frasa kata benda, bukan sebelum klausa lengkap.

common_mistakes.wrong: Although the strict requirements, hundreds applied.
common_mistakes.correct: Despite the strict requirements, hundreds applied.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Although' needs a clause; 'Despite' can take a noun phrase. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Although' memerlukan klausa; 'Despite' dapat diikuti frasa kata benda.

other_examples.sentence: 1. Despite the noise, he continued studying.
other_examples.translation: Meskipun ada kebisingan, dia terus belajar.

other_examples.sentence: 2. Despite her injury, she finished the race.
other_examples.translation: Meskipun cedera, dia menyelesaikan balapan.

questions.question: There are not ___ chairs available in the examination hall for all the students.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Many' is used with plural countable nouns such as 'chairs' in negative sentences. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Many' digunakan dengan kata benda jamak yang dapat dihitung seperti 'chairs' dalam kalimat negatif.
details_explanation.introduction: Countable and uncountable nouns take different quantifiers.

rules.title: 1. Many + Plural Countable Noun
rules.explanation: Use 'many' with plural countable nouns in questions and negatives.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'many' dengan kata benda jamak yang dapat dihitung dalam pertanyaan dan kalimat negatif.

common_mistakes.wrong: There are not much chairs.
common_mistakes.correct: There are not many chairs.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns, not plural countable nouns. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Much' digunakan dengan kata benda tak dapat dihitung, bukan kata benda jamak yang dapat dihitung.

other_examples.sentence: 1. There are not many books on the shelf.
other_examples.translation: Tidak banyak buku di rak.

other_examples.sentence: 2. We do not have many options.
other_examples.translation: Kami tidak memiliki banyak pilihan.

questions.question: The sun ___ in the east and sets in the west, which is a basic scientific fact.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The simple present 'rises' is used for general scientific truths, with singular subject 'sun'. Bahasa Indonesia: Simple present 'rises' digunakan untuk kebenaran ilmiah umum, dengan subjek tunggal 'sun'.
details_explanation.introduction: The simple present expresses facts that are generally true.

rules.title: 1. Simple Present for Facts
rules.explanation: Use the simple present for scientific facts and general truths.
notes: ID: Gunakan simple present untuk fakta ilmiah dan kebenaran umum.

common_mistakes.wrong: The sun rise in the east.
common_mistakes.correct: The sun rises in the east.
common_mistakes.reason: English: The singular subject 'sun' requires 'rises'. Bahasa Indonesia: Subjek tunggal 'sun' memerlukan 'rises'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
other_examples.translation: Air mendidih pada 100 derajat Celsius.

other_examples.sentence: 2. The earth revolves around the sun.
other_examples.translation: Bumi berputar mengelilingi matahari.

questions.question: We will visit the historical museum ___ we have free time this weekend.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'If' introduces a condition for a possible future event. Bahasa Indonesia: 'If' memperkenalkan kondisi untuk peristiwa masa depan yang mungkin terjadi.
details_explanation.introduction: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb.

rules.title: 1. If-Clause Condition
rules.explanation: Use 'if' to introduce a condition that must happen for the result to occur.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'if' untuk memperkenalkan kondisi yang harus terjadi agar hasilnya tercapai.

common_mistakes.wrong: We will visit if we will have free time.
common_mistakes.correct: We will visit if we have free time.
common_mistakes.reason: English: The if-clause uses the present simple, not 'will'. Bahasa Indonesia: Klausa if menggunakan present simple, bukan 'will'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. If it rains, we will stay at home.
other_examples.translation: Jika hujan, kita akan tinggal di rumah.

other_examples.sentence: 2. She will pass if she studies hard.
other_examples.translation: Dia akan lulus jika dia belajar keras.

questions.question: The candidate ___ won the student council election is my next-door neighbor.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Who' refers to a person and acts as the subject of the relative clause. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Who' merujuk pada orang dan berfungsi sebagai subjek relative clause.
details_explanation.introduction: Use 'who' for people, 'which' for things, and 'where' for places.

rules.title: 1. Who as Subject
rules.explanation: Use 'who' when the relative pronoun is the subject referring to a person.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'who' ketika relative pronoun adalah subjek yang merujuk pada orang.

common_mistakes.wrong: The candidate which won the election is my neighbor.
common_mistakes.correct: The candidate who won the election is my neighbor.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Which' refers to things, not people. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Which' merujuk benda, bukan orang.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The man who called you is my uncle.
other_examples.translation: Pria yang meneleponmu adalah pamanku.

other_examples.sentence: 2. The student who won the prize is here.
other_examples.translation: Siswa yang memenangkan hadiah itu ada di sini.

questions.question: The instructor spoke ___ so that all the recruits could hear the commands clearly.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Loudly' is an adverb of manner modifying 'spoke'. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Loudly' adalah adverb of manner yang memodifikasi 'spoke'.
details_explanation.introduction: Adverbs of manner describe how an action is done.

rules.title: 1. Adverb after Verb
rules.explanation: Use an adverb to modify the verb 'spoke'.
notes: ID: Gunakan adverb untuk memodifikasi kata kerja 'spoke'.

common_mistakes.wrong: The instructor spoke loud.
common_mistakes.correct: The instructor spoke loudly.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Loud' can be an adjective; the verb needs the adverb 'loudly'. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Loud' dapat berupa adjective; kata kerja memerlukan adverb 'loudly'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. She sang beautifully at the ceremony.
other_examples.translation: Dia bernyanyi dengan indah di upacara.

other_examples.sentence: 2. He answered the question correctly.
other_examples.translation: Dia menjawab pertanyaan itu dengan benar.

questions.question: The explanation given by the professor during the lecture was incredibly ___.

details_explanation.explanation: English: After the linking verb 'was', an adjective is needed to describe 'explanation'; 'helpful' is correct. Bahasa Indonesia: Setelah linking verb 'was', adjective diperlukan untuk menjelaskan 'explanation'; 'helpful' adalah bentuk yang tepat.
details_explanation.introduction: Linking verbs such as be, seem, and become are followed by adjectives, not adverbs.

rules.title: 1. Adjective after Linking Verb
rules.explanation: Use an adjective after a linking verb to describe the subject.
notes: ID: Gunakan adjective setelah linking verb untuk menjelaskan subjek.

common_mistakes.wrong: The explanation was incredibly helpfully.
common_mistakes.correct: The explanation was incredibly helpful.
common_mistakes.reason: English: A linking verb takes an adjective, not an adverb. Bahasa Indonesia: Linking verb diikuti adjective, bukan adverb.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The lecture was very helpful.
other_examples.translation: Kuliah itu sangat membantu.

other_examples.sentence: 2. Her advice seems useful.
other_examples.translation: Sarannya tampak berguna.

questions.question: The military cadets ___ currently marching in the main field under the hot sun.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The plural subject 'cadets' takes 'are' in the present continuous for an action happening now. Bahasa Indonesia: Subjek jamak 'cadets' memakai 'are' dalam present continuous untuk aksi yang sedang terjadi sekarang.
details_explanation.introduction: Present continuous: am/is/are + present participle.

rules.title: 1. Plural Subject in Present Continuous
rules.explanation: Use 'are' with plural subjects in the present continuous.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'are' dengan subjek jamak dalam present continuous.

common_mistakes.wrong: The cadets is marching now.
common_mistakes.correct: The cadets are marching now.
common_mistakes.reason: English: Plural 'cadets' requires 'are'. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Cadets' jamak memerlukan 'are'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The students are studying in the library.
other_examples.translation: Para siswa sedang belajar di perpustakaan.

other_examples.sentence: 2. They are training for the competition.
other_examples.translation: Mereka sedang berlatih untuk kompetisi.

questions.question: I have ___ my physical training for the police entrance exam.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The present perfect uses 'have + past participle'; 'completed' is the correct past participle. Bahasa Indonesia: Present perfect menggunakan 'have + past participle'; 'completed' adalah past participle yang tepat.
details_explanation.introduction: Present perfect: have/has + past participle.

rules.title: 1. Have + Past Participle
rules.explanation: Use the past participle after 'have' to describe a completed action with present relevance.
notes: ID: Gunakan past participle setelah 'have' untuk menyatakan aksi selesai yang relevan dengan sekarang.

common_mistakes.wrong: I have complete my training.
common_mistakes.correct: I have completed my training.
common_mistakes.reason: English: The present perfect needs the past participle 'completed'. Bahasa Indonesia: Present perfect memerlukan past participle 'completed'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. She has finished her homework.
other_examples.translation: Dia telah menyelesaikan pekerjaan rumahnya.

other_examples.sentence: 2. They have submitted the forms.
other_examples.translation: Mereka telah mengumpulkan formulirnya.

questions.question: ___! We finally passed the academic entrance test for the state university.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Hooray' expresses joy, approval, or celebration. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Hooray' mengekspresikan kegembiraan, persetujuan, atau perayaan.
details_explanation.introduction: Interjections can express celebration and positive emotion.

rules.title: 1. Hooray for Celebration
rules.explanation: Use 'Hooray' to celebrate success or good news.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'Hooray' untuk merayakan keberhasilan atau kabar baik.

common_mistakes.wrong: Alas! We passed the test.
common_mistakes.correct: Hooray! We passed the test.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Alas' expresses sorrow, not celebration. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Alas' mengekspresikan kesedihan, bukan perayaan.

other_examples.sentence: 1. Hooray! We won the match.
other_examples.translation: Hore! Kami memenangkan pertandingan.

other_examples.sentence: 2. Hooray! The exams are over.
other_examples.translation: Hore! Ujiannya sudah selesai.

questions.question: He wanted to join the state university, ___ he did not pass the selection test.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'But' connects a desire with an unexpected negative result. Bahasa Indonesia: 'But' menghubungkan keinginan dengan hasil negatif yang tidak terduga.
details_explanation.introduction: Use 'but' to show contrast between two clauses.

rules.title: 1. But for Contrast
rules.explanation: Use 'but' when the second clause contrasts with the first.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'but' ketika klausa kedua bertentangan dengan klausa pertama.

common_mistakes.wrong: He wanted to join, so he did not pass.
common_mistakes.correct: He wanted to join, but he did not pass.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'So' shows result, not contrast. Bahasa Indonesia: 'So' menunjukkan hasil, bukan kontras.

other_examples.sentence: 1. She wanted to go, but she was too tired.
other_examples.translation: Dia ingin pergi, tetapi dia terlalu lelah.

other_examples.sentence: 2. He studied hard, but he failed the test.
other_examples.translation: Dia belajar keras, tetapi dia gagal ujian.

questions.question: I need to buy ___ new notebooks for the upcoming semester at the state university.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'A few' is used with plural countable nouns in positive sentences. Bahasa Indonesia: 'A few' digunakan dengan kata benda jamak yang dapat dihitung dalam kalimat positif.
details_explanation.introduction: Quantifiers show quantity; a few is for countable nouns, a little for uncountable nouns.

rules.title: 1. A Few + Plural Countable Noun
rules.explanation: Use 'a few' before plural countable nouns to mean a small number.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'a few' sebelum kata benda jamak yang dapat dihitung untuk berarti sejumlah kecil.

common_mistakes.wrong: I need to buy a little notebooks.
common_mistakes.correct: I need to buy a few notebooks.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'A little' is for uncountable nouns; 'notebooks' is countable plural. Bahasa Indonesia: 'A little' untuk kata benda tak dapat dihitung; 'notebooks' adalah jamak yang dapat dihitung.

other_examples.sentence: 1. She bought a few apples.
other_examples.translation: Dia membeli beberapa apel.

other_examples.sentence: 2. We need a few chairs for the meeting.
other_examples.translation: Kami memerlukan beberapa kursi untuk rapat.

questions.question: The committee praised the debate team for their ___ performance in the national competition.

details_explanation.explanation: English: An adjective is needed to modify the noun 'performance'; 'outstanding' is correct. Bahasa Indonesia: Adjective diperlukan untuk memodifikasi kata benda 'performance'; 'outstanding' adalah bentuk yang tepat.
details_explanation.introduction: Adjectives describe nouns and usually come before the noun.

rules.title: 1. Adjective before Noun
rules.explanation: Use an adjective before the noun it describes.
notes: ID: Gunakan adjective sebelum kata benda yang dijelaskannya.

common_mistakes.wrong: Their outstandingly performance was praised.
common_mistakes.correct: Their outstanding performance was praised.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Outstandingly' is an adverb; the noun needs the adjective 'outstanding'. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Outstandingly' adalah adverb; kata benda memerlukan adjective 'outstanding'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. She gave an outstanding presentation.
other_examples.translation: Dia memberikan presentasi yang luar biasa.

other_examples.sentence: 2. The team showed outstanding courage.
other_examples.translation: Tim itu menunjukkan keberanian yang luar biasa.

questions.question: Neither the commander nor the soldiers ___ aware of the sudden change in the schedule.

details_explanation.explanation: English: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject; 'soldiers' is plural, so 'are' is correct. Bahasa Indonesia: Dengan 'neither...nor', kata kerja sesuai dengan subjek terdekat; 'soldiers' jamak, jadi 'are' tepat.
details_explanation.introduction: Neither...nor follows the proximity rule for subject-verb agreement.

rules.title: 1. Proximity Rule
rules.explanation: The verb agrees with the subject closest to it after 'nor'.
notes: ID: Kata kerja sesuai dengan subjek yang paling dekat setelah 'nor'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Neither the commander nor the soldiers is aware.
common_mistakes.correct: Neither the commander nor the soldiers are aware.
common_mistakes.reason: English: The nearer subject 'soldiers' is plural, requiring 'are'. Bahasa Indonesia: Subjek terdekat 'soldiers' jamak, memerlukan 'are'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. Neither the teacher nor the students are ready.
other_examples.translation: Baik guru maupun para siswa belum siap.

other_examples.sentence: 2. Neither the boys nor the girl is here.
other_examples.translation: Baik anak laki-laki maupun anak perempuan itu tidak ada di sini.

questions.question: We have ___ completed the registration process for the police academy.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Just' is used in positive present perfect sentences for an action completed a very short time ago. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Just' digunakan dalam kalimat present perfect positif untuk aksi yang selesai sangat baru-baru ini.
details_explanation.introduction: Just, already, and yet are common present perfect adverbs.

rules.title: 1. Just + Past Participle
rules.explanation: Place 'just' between 'have/has' and the past participle.
notes: ID: Letakkan 'just' di antara 'have/has' dan past participle.

common_mistakes.wrong: We have yet completed the process.
common_mistakes.correct: We have just completed the process.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Yet' is usually used in negatives/questions; 'just' fits this positive sentence. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Yet' biasanya untuk negatif/pertanyaan; 'just' cocok untuk kalimat positif ini.

other_examples.sentence: 1. She has just arrived.
other_examples.translation: Dia baru saja tiba.

other_examples.sentence: 2. They have just finished the exam.
other_examples.translation: Mereka baru saja menyelesaikan ujian.

questions.question: The government is implementing new ___ policies to protect the remaining forests in Indonesia.

details_explanation.explanation: English: An adjective is needed to modify 'policies'; 'environmental' is the correct adjective. Bahasa Indonesia: Adjective diperlukan untuk memodifikasi 'policies'; 'environmental' adalah adjective yang tepat.
details_explanation.introduction: Adjectives describe nouns and can be formed with suffixes such as -al.

rules.title: 1. Adjective before Noun
rules.explanation: Use an adjective before the noun it modifies.
notes: ID: Gunakan adjective sebelum kata benda yang dimodifikasinya.

common_mistakes.wrong: The government is implementing new environment policies.
common_mistakes.correct: The government is implementing new environmental policies.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Environment' is a noun; 'environmental' is the adjective. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Environment' adalah kata benda; 'environmental' adalah adjective.

other_examples.sentence: 1. Environmental issues are important.
other_examples.translation: Masalah lingkungan itu penting.

other_examples.sentence: 2. They support environmental protection.
other_examples.translation: Mereka mendukung perlindungan lingkungan.

questions.question: My sister is as ___ as a bee when she is preparing for her final university exams.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The equative structure 'as ... as' uses the base adjective; 'busy' is correct. Bahasa Indonesia: Struktur equative 'as ... as' menggunakan adjective dasar; 'busy' adalah bentuk yang tepat.
details_explanation.introduction: Equative comparisons use as + adjective + as.

rules.title: 1. As + Adjective + As
rules.explanation: Use the base form of the adjective between 'as ... as'.
notes: ID: Gunakan bentuk dasar adjective di antara 'as ... as'.

common_mistakes.wrong: She is as busier as a bee.
common_mistakes.correct: She is as busy as a bee.
common_mistakes.reason: English: The equative uses the base adjective, not the comparative. Bahasa Indonesia: Equative menggunakan adjective dasar, bukan bentuk komparatif.

other_examples.sentence: 1. He is as tall as his father.
other_examples.translation: Dia setinggi ayahnya.

other_examples.sentence: 2. This room is as clean as that one.
other_examples.translation: Ruangan ini sebersih ruangan itu.

questions.question: The headmaster is directly responsible ___ maintaining the school's discipline and order.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The adjective 'responsible' is followed by 'for' to show accountability. Bahasa Indonesia: Adjective 'responsible' diikuti 'for' untuk menunjukkan tanggung jawab.
details_explanation.introduction: Some adjectives have fixed prepositions, such as responsible for and interested in.

rules.title: 1. Responsible For
rules.explanation: Use 'responsible for' before a noun or gerund showing what someone is accountable for.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'responsible for' sebelum kata benda atau gerund yang menunjukkan tanggung jawab.

common_mistakes.wrong: She is responsible on maintaining discipline.
common_mistakes.correct: She is responsible for maintaining discipline.
common_mistakes.reason: English: The fixed preposition after 'responsible' is 'for'. Bahasa Indonesia: Preposisi tetap setelah 'responsible' adalah 'for'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The manager is responsible for the team.
other_examples.translation: Manajer bertanggung jawab atas tim itu.

other_examples.sentence: 2. Parents are responsible for their children's safety.
other_examples.translation: Orang tua bertanggung jawab atas keselamatan anak-anak mereka.

questions.question: The applicants must submit their official ___ before the strict deadline.

details_explanation.explanation: English: A noun is needed as the object of 'submit'; 'application' is the noun form. Bahasa Indonesia: Kata benda diperlukan sebagai objek dari 'submit'; 'application' adalah bentuk kata bendanya.
details_explanation.introduction: The suffix -ation can form nouns from verbs.

rules.title: 1. Noun as Object
rules.explanation: Use a noun after the verb 'submit'.
notes: ID: Gunakan kata benda setelah kata kerja 'submit'.

common_mistakes.wrong: The applicants must submit their apply.
common_mistakes.correct: The applicants must submit their application.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Apply' is a verb; 'application' is the noun. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Apply' adalah kata kerja; 'application' adalah kata benda.

other_examples.sentence: 1. Please submit your application by Friday.
other_examples.translation: Silakan kumpulkan lamaran Anda sebelum Jumat.

other_examples.sentence: 2. The application was accepted.
other_examples.translation: Lamaran itu diterima.

questions.question: The teacher gave ___ a special assignment to help improve his English writing skills.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Gave' needs an indirect object pronoun; 'him' is the correct object form. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Gave' memerlukan indirect object pronoun; 'him' adalah bentuk objek yang tepat.
details_explanation.introduction: Indirect object pronouns receive the thing being given.

rules.title: 1. Him as Indirect Object
rules.explanation: Use 'him' for a male singular indirect object.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'him' untuk indirect object tunggal laki-laki.

common_mistakes.wrong: The teacher gave he an assignment.
common_mistakes.correct: The teacher gave him an assignment.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'He' is a subject pronoun; 'him' is the object pronoun. Bahasa Indonesia: 'He' adalah subject pronoun; 'him' adalah object pronoun.

other_examples.sentence: 1. She gave him a book.
other_examples.translation: Dia memberinya sebuah buku.

other_examples.sentence: 2. We sent him the documents.
other_examples.translation: Kami mengiriminya dokumen-dokumen itu.

questions.question: The instructions provided in the examination manual are very ___.

details_explanation.explanation: English: After the linking verb 'are', an adjective is needed; 'clear' is correct. Bahasa Indonesia: Setelah linking verb 'are', adjective diperlukan; 'clear' adalah bentuk yang tepat.
details_explanation.introduction: Linking verbs are followed by adjectives that describe the subject.

rules.title: 1. Adjective after Are
rules.explanation: Use an adjective after 'are' to describe 'instructions'.
notes: ID: Gunakan adjective setelah 'are' untuk menjelaskan 'instructions'.

common_mistakes.wrong: The instructions are very clearly.
common_mistakes.correct: The instructions are very clear.
common_mistakes.reason: English: A linking verb takes an adjective, not an adverb. Bahasa Indonesia: Linking verb diikuti adjective, bukan adverb.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The rules are clear.
other_examples.translation: Peraturannya jelas.

other_examples.sentence: 2. Her explanation was very clear.
other_examples.translation: Penjelasannya sangat jelas.

questions.question: She ___ her student ID card, so she cannot enter the examination room right now.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The present perfect 'has lost' shows a past action with a present result: she cannot enter now. Bahasa Indonesia: Present perfect 'has lost' menunjukkan aksi masa lalu dengan hasil sekarang: dia tidak bisa masuk sekarang.
details_explanation.introduction: The present perfect connects a past action to a present result.

rules.title: 1. Present Result
rules.explanation: Use the present perfect when the result of a past action affects the present.
notes: ID: Gunakan present perfect ketika hasil aksi masa lalu memengaruhi masa kini.

common_mistakes.wrong: She lost her card, so she cannot enter now.
common_mistakes.correct: She has lost her card, so she cannot enter now.
common_mistakes.reason: English: The present perfect better emphasizes the present result. Bahasa Indonesia: Present perfect lebih menekankan hasil saat ini.

other_examples.sentence: 1. He has broken his leg, so he cannot walk.
other_examples.translation: Dia telah mematahkan kakinya, jadi dia tidak bisa berjalan.

other_examples.sentence: 2. They have missed the bus, so they are late.
other_examples.translation: Mereka telah ketinggalan bus, jadi mereka terlambat.

questions.question: The university applicant ___ his documents carefully before submitting them.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The singular subject 'applicant' takes 'checks' in the simple present for a habitual action. Bahasa Indonesia: Subjek tunggal 'applicant' memakai 'checks' dalam simple present untuk tindakan kebiasaan.
details_explanation.introduction: The simple present describes habits and routines.

rules.title: 1. Third-Person Singular -s
rules.explanation: Add -s to the base verb with a singular third-person subject.
notes: ID: Tambahkan -s pada kata kerja dasar dengan subjek tunggal orang ketiga.

common_mistakes.wrong: The applicant check his documents.
common_mistakes.correct: The applicant checks his documents.
common_mistakes.reason: English: The singular subject requires 'checks'. Bahasa Indonesia: Subjek tunggal memerlukan 'checks'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The student checks his answers before submitting.
other_examples.translation: Siswa itu memeriksa jawabannya sebelum mengumpulkan.

other_examples.sentence: 2. She reads the instructions carefully.
other_examples.translation: Dia membaca instruksinya dengan hati-hati.

questions.question: If the weather is bad tomorrow, the outdoor military drill ___ cancelled.

details_explanation.explanation: English: In a first conditional, the main clause uses 'will + base verb' for a likely future result. Bahasa Indonesia: Dalam first conditional, main clause menggunakan 'will + kata kerja dasar' untuk hasil masa depan yang mungkin terjadi.
details_explanation.introduction: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb.

rules.title: 1. Will in Main Clause
rules.explanation: Use 'will be' in the result clause of a first conditional.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'will be' dalam klausa hasil pada first conditional.

common_mistakes.wrong: If the weather is bad, the drill would be cancelled.
common_mistakes.correct: If the weather is bad, the drill will be cancelled.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Would' is for second conditional; first conditional uses 'will'. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Would' untuk second conditional; first conditional menggunakan 'will'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. If it rains, the event will be postponed.
other_examples.translation: Jika hujan, acara akan ditunda.

other_examples.sentence: 2. If you study hard, you will pass.
other_examples.translation: Jika kamu belajar keras, kamu akan lulus.

questions.question: He is the ___ student in the entire military high school due to his perfect attendance.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Most disciplined' is the superlative form comparing one student with the whole school. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Most disciplined' adalah bentuk superlatif yang membandingkan satu siswa dengan seluruh sekolah.
details_explanation.introduction: Superlatives compare one person or thing with a whole group.

rules.title: 1. The Most + Adjective
rules.explanation: Use 'the most + adjective' for superlative comparisons with longer adjectives.
rules.structure: the most + adjective + noun + in + group
notes: ID: Gunakan 'the most + adjective' untuk perbandingan superlatif dengan adjective yang lebih panjang.

common_mistakes.wrong: He is the more disciplined student in the school.
common_mistakes.correct: He is the most disciplined student in the school.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'More' is comparative; 'most' is superlative. Bahasa Indonesia: 'More' adalah komparatif; 'most' adalah superlatif.

other_examples.sentence: 1. She is the most disciplined member of the team.
other_examples.translation: Dia adalah anggota tim yang paling disiplin.

other_examples.sentence: 2. This is the most difficult exam.
other_examples.translation: Ini adalah ujian yang paling sulit.

questions.question: The mysterious ___ of the confidential files caused a major security breach at the office.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Disappearance' is the noun meaning the act of vanishing; it fits after the adjective 'mysterious'. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Disappearance' adalah kata benda yang berarti tindakan menghilang; cocok setelah adjective 'mysterious'.
details_explanation.introduction: A noun is needed after an adjective and before 'of'.

rules.title: 1. Noun + Of
rules.explanation: Use a noun before 'of' to name the event or thing involved.
notes: ID: Gunakan kata benda sebelum 'of' untuk menyebut peristiwa atau hal yang terlibat.

common_mistakes.wrong: The mysterious disappear of the files...
common_mistakes.correct: The mysterious disappearance of the files...
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Disappear' is a verb; 'disappearance' is the noun. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Disappear' adalah kata kerja; 'disappearance' adalah kata benda.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The disappearance of the money is still a mystery.
other_examples.translation: Hilangnya uang itu masih menjadi misteri.

other_examples.sentence: 2. They reported the disappearance of the documents.
other_examples.translation: Mereka melaporkan hilangnya dokumen-dokumen itu.

questions.question: The judge handed ___ the final verdict after a long and careful deliberation.

details_explanation.explanation: English: 'Handed' needs an indirect object pronoun; 'him' is the correct object form. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Handed' memerlukan indirect object pronoun; 'him' adalah bentuk objek yang tepat.
details_explanation.introduction: Verbs like hand, give, and send can take an indirect object pronoun.

rules.title: 1. Indirect Object Pronoun
rules.explanation: Use an object pronoun to show the recipient of the verdict.
notes: ID: Gunakan object pronoun untuk menunjukkan penerima vonis.

common_mistakes.wrong: The judge handed he the verdict.
common_mistakes.correct: The judge handed him the verdict.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'He' is a subject pronoun; 'him' is the object pronoun. Bahasa Indonesia: 'He' adalah subject pronoun; 'him' adalah object pronoun.

other_examples.sentence: 1. The clerk handed him the form.
other_examples.translation: Petugas menyerahkan formulir itu kepadanya.

questions.question: My older brother ___ to the city library every weekend to prepare for his university exams.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The third-person singular subject 'brother' requires 'goes' in the simple present for a routine. Bahasa Indonesia: Subjek tunggal orang ketiga 'brother' memerlukan 'goes' dalam simple present untuk rutinitas.
details_explanation.introduction: The simple present is used for regular routines and habits.

rules.title: 1. Go → Goes
rules.explanation: Add -es to 'go' with he, she, it, or a singular noun.
notes: ID: Tambahkan -es pada 'go' dengan he, she, it, atau kata benda tunggal.

common_mistakes.wrong: My older brother go to the library every weekend.
common_mistakes.correct: My older brother goes to the library every weekend.
common_mistakes.reason: English: The singular subject requires 'goes'. Bahasa Indonesia: Subjek tunggal memerlukan 'goes'.

other_examples.sentence: 1. He goes to school by bus.
other_examples.translation: Dia pergi ke sekolah dengan bus.

other_examples.sentence: 2. She goes to the gym every morning.
other_examples.translation: Dia pergi ke gym setiap pagi.

questions.question: This is the ___ opportunity you will ever get to study at a top state university.

details_explanation.explanation: English: The superlative form of 'good' is 'best', showing the highest quality among all possibilities. Bahasa Indonesia: Bentuk superlatif dari 'good' adalah 'best', menunjukkan kualitas tertinggi di antara semua kemungkinan.
details_explanation.introduction: Irregular adjectives have special comparative and superlative forms: good → better → best.

rules.title: 1. Good → Best
rules.explanation: Use 'best' as the superlative form of 'good'.
notes: ID: Gunakan 'best' sebagai bentuk superlatif dari 'good'.

common_mistakes.wrong: This is the bestest opportunity.
common_mistakes.correct: This is the best opportunity.
common_mistakes.reason: English: 'Best' is already superlative; 'bestest' is nonstandard. Bahasa Indonesia: 'Best' sudah superlatif; 'bestest' tidak baku.
